FILES: `scripts/local_agent_git.py` (production, 156 lines - append only, at the END of the file). New test file `tests/unit/test_step_cap_auto_done.py`.

WHAT TO BUILD - append exactly these two functions (and one module constant) to the END of `scripts/local_agent_git.py`. Do not edit anything above them.

```python
_TEST_FILE_PREFIXES = ("test_",)


def _changed_production_paths(paths: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Return the entries of ``paths`` that are production files.

    A path is NOT production when it is empty, lies under a ``tests/``
    directory at any depth, has a basename starting with ``test_`` or equal
    to ``conftest.py``, or has any path component starting with ``.`` (the
    agent's runtime artifacts: ``.agent_scratchpad.md``,
    ``.agent_transcript.json``, ``.dispatch_baseline_test_checked``).
    Order is preserved.
    """


def _step_cap_auto_done_impl(origin) -> bool:
    """Whether a run that reached the step cap already finished its work.

    True only when BOTH hold:
    1. the branch changes at least one production file relative to its
       merge-base with the default branch, and
    2. ``origin["_full_suite_result"]()`` reports the full suite and lint
       green (its first tuple element is truthy).
    Fails closed: any unresolvable base or git error returns False.
    """
```

Behavior of `_step_cap_auto_done_impl(origin)`:
- `origin` is the calling agent module's `globals()` (same routing convention as the other `*_impl` functions in this file - read its module docstring). Use `origin["git"](*args)`, which returns an object with `.returncode` and `.stdout`, and `origin["_full_suite_result"]()`, which returns `(ok: bool, tail: str, gate: str | None)`.
- Resolve the base: try, in order, `origin["git"]("merge-base", "HEAD", ref)` for ref in `("origin/HEAD", "origin/main", "origin/master", "main", "master")`; use the first with `returncode == 0` and non-empty stripped stdout. If none works, return False.
- `origin["git"]("diff", "--name-only", base, "HEAD")`; non-zero returncode -> False. Split stdout into lines, strip each, pass to `_changed_production_paths`; an empty result -> False (do NOT run the suite in that case).
- Otherwise return `bool(origin["_full_suite_result"]()[0])`.
- Wrap the whole body so any exception returns False.

TDD - write `tests/unit/test_step_cap_auto_done.py` FIRST and confirm it fails (ImportError on the new names is the expected red). Build a fake `origin` dict in the test: `"git"` is a function that looks up a canned result by `args[0]` (e.g. a `types.SimpleNamespace(returncode=..., stdout=...)`), and `"_full_suite_result"` is a stub that records whether it was called. Do not start real git or pytest subprocesses. Cover:
- `_changed_production_paths`: keeps `pipeline/x.py` and `README.md`; drops `tests/unit/test_x.py`, `pkg/tests/helper.py`, `test_top.py`, `pkg/conftest.py`, `.agent_scratchpad.md`, `a/.hidden/b.py`, and `""`; preserves input order; empty list -> empty list.
- auto-done True: base resolves via `origin/HEAD`, diff lists one production file, suite stub returns `(True, "", None)`.
- False when the suite stub returns `(False, "tail", "test")`, and when it returns `(False, "tail", "lint")`.
- False, and the suite stub is NEVER called, when the diff lists only test files / only dotfiles / nothing.
- base falls back to `master` when every earlier ref returns returncode 128.
- False when no ref resolves (all 128), and when the diff call returns non-zero.
- False (no exception) when the git stub raises `OSError`.

def _keyless_reingest_error(
    plan: dict, only_epics: list[str] | None, already_ingested: bool, overwrite: bool
) -> str | None:
    """Error text when re-ingesting would mint duplicate stories, else None.

    Without an explicit ``key`` a story is keyed by a fresh UUID (or a new
    ticket id) on every ingest, so re-ingesting a plan whose manifest already
    exists adds a second copy of that story next to the first, and both

stories.summary: Resolve a story's bare registry model name to its tag instead of silently falling back to the default local model
stories.description: LD90 W5 pin-drop investigation, root cause found: story 22b78cd3 pinned `deepseek-v4.1-flash` (a registry model NAME, not a tag). app/ollama_prompt_utils.py::_resolve_local_model treats any value without ':' or '/' as a tier name and returns PIPELINE_LOCAL_MODEL_DEFAULT (gpt-oss-20b-high) for an unknown one, so the pin was silently ignored. Resolve a bare name through the live registry's providers.<provider>.models catalog first.

Preflight: impact run 2026-09-23 on 0bdf7fe — 1 conflict (test_readme_reference_split.py::test_moved_section_body_is_verbatim[Plan / story schema]) re-scoped: doc goes in a new section outside the pinned one; re-run clean (12567 passed, ruff clean).
Tier: cloud open-source.

FILES: `pipeline/dispatch_routing.py` (188 lines), `REFERENCE.md` (docs). New test file `tests/unit/test_dispatch_model_pin_registry_name.py`.

ROOT CAUSE (already diagnosed - do not re-investigate): `_resolve_dispatch_target` returns `story["model"]` verbatim. A value like `"deepseek-v4.1-flash"` (no `:` or `/`) is later passed to `app/ollama_prompt_utils.py::_resolve_local_model`, which only knows the tiers `opus|sonnet|haiku` and returns the default local model for anything else. The registry (`role_registry.load_registry()["providers"][<provider>]["models"][<name>]["tag"]`) maps `deepseek-v4.1-flash` -> `deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud`.

EDIT 1 - add a helper to `pipeline/dispatch_routing.py`, immediately BEFORE `def _resolve_dispatch_target(`:

```python
def _registry_tag_for(provider: str, model: str) -> str:
    """Translate a bare registry model NAME to its concrete tag.

    ``model`` is returned unchanged when it already looks like a tag
    (contains ':' or '/'), or when the live registry has no
    ``providers.<provider>.models.<model>.tag`` entry, or when the registry
    cannot be loaded. A bare name that is neither a registry name nor one of
    the tier names ``opus``/``sonnet``/``haiku`` is logged as a warning,
    because the local driver would otherwise run the default model instead.
    """
```

Use `role_registry.load_registry()`; catch `role_registry.RoleRegistryError` and `KeyError`/`TypeError` (fail open to returning `model`). Warn with `logging.getLogger("pipeline").warning(...)` naming the model and provider, never raise.

EDIT 2 - in `_resolve_dispatch_target`, find the exact two lines

```python
    provider = _resolve_dispatch_backend(story, resolution.provider)
    model = story.get("model")
```

and change the second line to

```python
    model = story.get("model")
    if model:
        model = _registry_tag_for(provider, model)
```

Do NOT apply it on the `except role_registry.RoleRegistryError:` fail-open branch above (that branch returns no model at all today - keep it).

EDIT 3 - `REFERENCE.md`: do NOT edit the `## Plan / story schema` section (including its `model` bullet) - its body is pinned verbatim by `tests/unit/test_readme_reference_split.py::test_moved_section_body_is_verbatim`. Instead insert a NEW section immediately before the exact heading line `## Per-role provider/model configuration`:

```
## Story model pins

A story's `model` may be a Claude tier (`opus | sonnet | haiku`), a
concrete model tag (e.g. `glm-5.3-flash:cloud`), or a model name declared
in the live registry's `providers.<provider>.models` (e.g.
`deepseek-v4.1-flash`). Dispatch resolves a registry name to that entry's
`tag` for the provider the story dispatches on. A bare name that is none of
these is logged as a warning, because the local driver would otherwise run
its default model instead of the pin.

```

Touch nothing else in REFERENCE.md.

TDD - write the test file FIRST; stub the registry at its boundary by monkeypatching `pipeline.dispatch_routing.role_registry.load_registry` to return a synthetic dict (never assert against the real `model_registry*.json` - see .claude/rules/testing-config-gates.md). `_registry_tag_for`: bare declared name -> its tag; `"x:cloud"` unchanged and registry not consulted; `"openai/gpt"` unchanged; unknown bare name unchanged + a warning logged (use `caplog`); `"sonnet"` with no registry entry unchanged and NO warning; provider missing from registry -> unchanged; `load_registry` raising `RoleRegistryError` -> unchanged. `_resolve_dispatch_target`: with `resolve_role` stubbed to return provider `"ollama"`, a story `{"model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash"}` resolves to `("ollama", "deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud")`; a story with no model still gets the resolved role model.

stories.summary: Stop the workspace-listing test from racing git's background auto-maintenance
stories.description: LD90 W5 flake quarantine. The only flake in the last 60 master CI runs: run 35676554190 (Python 3.12, ubuntu) failed tests/unit/test_service_workspace.py::test_list_workspaces_recorded_path_with_git_dir_removed_is_invalid_but_exists with FileNotFoundError inside shutil.rmtree(repo/'.git') on .git/objects - consistent with git's post-commit auto-maintenance writing into .git while rmtree walks it. Disable auto-maintenance in the file's repo helper. Test-only change.

stories.summary: After a rework redispatch that produced no new commit, start the next one from a fresh context with a root-cause diagnosis
stories.description: LD90 W6. 'No new commit after N rework redispatches' parked or escalated 16 stories since 9/16. Each no-progress redispatch currently resumes the same cluttered transcript with no new diagnosis. On the first no-commit round, drop the transcript (so the next rework is a cold, from-brief start at the last commit) and fold a CLAUDE.md Step 9 diagnosis into the brief, reusing the step-cap rebrief path.
